name: Augustiner-Museum Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Augustinian Museum in Rattenberg: a high-class sacred art museum in the Gothic Augustinian monastery from 1385 with an accessible church tower.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Augustinian Museum in Rattenberg, Austria's smallest municipality, is an outstanding cultural gem housed within the venerable historic monastery walls of the former Augustinian Hermitage. Founded in the late 14th century by the art-loving Lords of Freundsberg as a spiritual center, the listed ensemble now houses one of the most significant collections of sacred art treasures in the entire Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley. The precious exhibits include Gothic wooden sculptures, Baroque altarpieces, valuable goldsmith work, processional crosses, and masterful liturgical vestments, vividly reflecting the religious devotion, popular piety, and craftsmanship traditions of the Inn Valley over many centuries.

Route & Requirements

The visitor-friendly museum tour leads guests through the atmospheric Gothic monastery church, the spacious cloister, and up historical staircases into the various thematic exhibition rooms. An absolute highlight of the tour is the secured ascent to the accessible church tower: solid wooden and metal stairs lead to the viewing platform, which offers a breathtaking panoramic view over the historic conglomerate roofs of the medieval glass town, the mighty Inn River, and the rocky backdrop of the Brandenberg Alps. The exhibition areas on the ground floor are barrier-free; for the tower ascent, a head for heights and surefootedness are recommended.

Visit & Arrival

The Augustinian Museum, popular and highly regarded far beyond national borders, opens its doors reliably during the summer months from May to the end of October daily from 10:00 to 17:00 for visitors from all over the world. Adults pay a regular admission price of approximately 7 Euros, while reduced rates are offered for seniors, young people, school classes, and family groups, and children under six years of age enjoy free admission. Arrival by public transport is extremely uncomplicated: Rattenberg-Kramsach train station is only a five-minute, flat walk from the museum entrance. Car drivers use the Inntal motorway A12 to the Kramsach exit and continue towards Breitenbach, parking their vehicles in the well-signposted large car parks directly in front of the historic gates of the traffic-calmed old town.

Tips

Be sure to combine your tour of the Augustinian Museum with an extended stroll through the picturesque pedestrian streets of Rattenberg. The traditional town is world-famous for its glass art; in numerous open workshops, you can watch glassblowers, engravers, and glass grinders at their delicate craft. To round off your cultural excursion, the traditional Hacker patisserie in the heart of the old town invites you to enjoy original Tyrolean pastries, homemade cakes, and freshly brewed coffee in a historic atmosphere.
preis: Adults approx. €8.00, children under 18 free; with Alpbachtal Card free of charge
